purpose: The OPERATIONAL view: what a driver may rely on, right now, on this host. Kept separate from primitives/harness-matrix.json, which is aesop's historical PRODUCT-support matrix pinned at a stated commit and is not rewritten here. Each capability carries three independent answers -- does the product support it, has polytropos implemented it, has anyone verified it by running it -- because collapsing them into one boolean is how a driver comes to believe it holds a control it does not.
unknown_is_valid: A capability nobody has run reports verified=unknown, and a caller needing certainty must treat that as no. Filling these in optimistically would make the file worse than not having it.

dispatch.note: one authorized live `bin/claude_execute.py run` on 2026-09-16 (UTC) against a one-task kit in a throwaway project on the maintainer's macOS 14.4 host, run 2026-09-16-60c2 in an explicit --attempt-store: `claude -p --model <sonnet-tier id from data/pricing.json> --dangerously-skip-permissions <prompt>` returned rc 0 in ~20 s, the one-line edit the brief asked for landed and nothing else changed, the task was projected done with no escalation. The 2026-09-06 verification (flag handling only) is superseded. Tests never invoke the real CLI

durable_attempts.note: polytropos capability, not a product one. Live on 2026-09-16 (the run above): claim.taken, run.started, roster.checked, verify.precheck, attempt.started, attempt.finished, verify.finished, task.projected, run.finished, claim.released were recorded outside the tree, and the review's attempt (run 2026-09-16-2c48, role reviewer) likewise. The dead-run path -- an open attempt closed as unknown and reconciled by re-running the check -- was exercised with stub executables and temp stores only. `duration_s` was null on both live attempts: the drivers' runners drop proc_runner's timing (follow-up)

tool_pin.note: the `--allowedTools=<space-joined>` form is REQUIRED: the variadic form swallows the following positional, which silently consumed the prompt on every review dispatch (found 2026-09-06). Re-verified 2026-09-16: `review --phase 1` dispatched `claude -p '--allowedTools=Bash Read Grep Glob' <prompt>` with no blanket grant, the reviewer received the prompt (it produced a phase review and a `REVIEW VERDICT=` line) and the tree was byte-identical afterwards. This row is why the registry has a verified column

confined_verify.note: polytropos capability, not a product one: verify commands run under an OS boundary. Re-verified 2026-09-16 in the live run above with the default `--exec-mode enforced`: `exec_policy check` reported the sandbox-exec backend, the precheck was red (rc 1) before the dispatch and the verify green (rc 0) after it, and enforced mode refuses rather than downgrading when no backend exists. macOS only -- enforced mode refuses on Linux and Windows. The ledger's verify events do not yet record which mode ran (follow-up)

confined_dispatch.note: sandbox-exec blocks Keychain access and subscription credentials live there, so a confined dispatch reports 'Not logged in'. Keychain access is gated by entitlements, not profile rules; granting mach-lookup and keychain writes does not change it

status.note: no run-status query is implemented here, and whether the CLI exposes one has not been checked

cancel.note: the process tree can be terminated; that says nothing about whether the model call it made was already billed

independent_review.note: phase-end review dispatched with a restricted permission profile and recorded in the attempt ledger. Live on 2026-09-16: `review --phase 1` on the throwaway kit returned rc 0 in ~40 s with `REVIEW VERDICT=accept`, was recorded as run 2026-09-16-2c48 role=reviewer op=review, and left the tree byte-identical. The review argv pins no model (`model: null` in the ledger; the CLI's default ran) and plain-text output attests none (`observed_model: null`); the verdict line is recorded beside the grade, never as it

effort_per_turn.note: changing reasoning effort between turns of one session with the cached prefix intact. Distinct from per-dispatch effort, which the driver sets once on the command line before the run starts and never changes afterwards

dispatch.note: bin/cursor_execute.py run through bin/cursor_adapter.build_dispatch; tests stub the binary. Verified 2026-09-16 on a real, logged-in install (macOS 14.4): one `run --task T1 --exec-mode enforced` on a throwaway one-task kit dispatched `agent -p --trust --workspace … --output-format json --force <prompt>` with no model pinned, rc 0 in ~17 s, the one-line edit landed and nothing else changed, the confined verify passed, T1 was projected done (run 2026-09-16-f427). Earlier the same day, logged out, the same command was refused with `Authentication required`, classified `auth`, and spent nothing (run 2026-09-16-765a)

identity_probe.note: polytropos capability: the generically named `agent` is dispatched to only after `--version` or `about --format json` identifies Cursor; unknown or absent fails closed. Verified 2026-09-16 on a real install (cliVersion 2026.09.10-fd3934a, macOS 14.4): earlier that day the binary was absent and the probe refused (`absent`); after `curl https://cursor.com/install -fsS | bash` the probe refused again (`unknown`), because the real CLI names itself nowhere -- `--version` prints a bare version and `about --format json` carries `cliVersion`, `latestStatus`, `latestVersion`, `osPlatform`, `model`, `subscriptionTier`, `userEmail`, ... with no product name in any value. The rule now accepts that schema with a string `cliVersion` (`cursor_adapter.ABOUT_SCHEMA_KEYS`), and `cursor_execute.py probe` answers `cursor (2026.09.10-fd3934a)` on this host. Only the version is kept from the payload

read_only_dispatch.note: review and verification dispatches pass --mode ask and never --force. Verified 2026-09-16: the documented smoke returned `ready` in 4 s, and `review --phase 1` ran ~80 s under `--mode ask` and left the tree byte-identical; the reviewer's own text says it could not run the verify command in ask mode ("switch to Agent mode or allow Shell"), which is the product refusing execution, observed once. Whether ask mode refuses every write on every prompt is still the product's promise

model_selection.note: --model is passed as written; the host's list is read at run time and never mirrored into a pricing file

structured_events.note: `--output-format json` verified 2026-09-16: a single JSON object per run with keys type, subtype, is_error, duration_ms, duration_api_ms, result, session_id, request_id, usage (inputTokens, outputTokens, cacheReadTokens, cacheWriteTokens). No `model` field, so the observed model stays unknown by design; `about` reports the selection as `Auto`. Only `result` and a string `model` are read; everything else stays unknown

status.note: `status` reports authentication, not a run; `ls`/`resume` address chats. No per-run status is exposed, so the adapter raises CapabilityError. 2026-09-16: `agent status` on a real install prints `Not logged in`, confirming it reports authentication, not a run

cancel.note: no documented way to cancel a run from outside it; bin/proc_runner.py can stop the process tree, which says nothing about whether the call was billed

cli_sandbox.note: Cursor's own command sandbox is documented and not relied on: verification runs under bin/exec_policy.py, and the dispatch itself is unconfined, as on every harness

usage_report.note: 2026-09-16: the CLI's `--output-format json` result carries a `usage` block (inputTokens, outputTokens, cacheReadTokens, cacheWriteTokens) and `duration_ms`, so the product does report usage; this adapter does not read it yet (follow-up) and prices nothing (data/pricing.cursor.json is an empty roster), so every Cursor dispatch stays unpriced (usd null). state.vscdb is an undocumented SQLite store this repository does not open
